OAP runs your apps on your own server, operated by your AI agent.

the server's IP address, its username and its password.

Server root@203.0.113.5: Ubuntu 18.04.2 LTS, x86_64, 1 CPU, 985 MiB memory, 12.1 GiB disk free
  ✓ connect   → check   · fix   · install   · owner account   · hand off

✗ Ubuntu 18.04.2 LTS: needs Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04, or Debian 12.
  Reinstall the server with Ubuntu 24.04 from your provider's console, then run oap again. OAP doesn't upgrade an operating system in place.
! 985 MiB memory, no swap: needs swap on servers under 2 GB.
  Add a 1 GiB swap file so a memory spike slows the server instead of stopping apps.
  Fix (routine): Create /swapfile (1 GiB), enable it and add it to /etc/fstab.
! Docker runs from /opt/docker-27.5.1/docker/dockerd, which no package manages; systemd drop-ins: oap-test-engine.conf: needs Docker Engine installed from a package, so it gets security updates.
  Replace it with Docker Engine from Docker's official package repository. Its containers restart.
  Fix (sensitive): Install Docker Engine from Docker's apt repository in place of the unmanaged one; running containers restart.

  Nothing to do. OAP leaves software it didn't install alone.
~ SSH accepts passwords, including for root.
  At hand-off, OAP offers to turn off password login once your own key works.
